revised_statement: DAF establishment intake MUST collect only the facts required by (a) each participant role's classified checks under RR-UNB-PART-007-r1, (b) the fund's program terms and (c) the first funding method. Every field for which Unbound already holds a fact about the same PartyId with freshness Fresh for that purpose (UNB-XIN-CLM-003), or which a configured verified identity provider supplies, MUST be prefilled and shown for confirmation rather than re-entered. Intake MUST support save-and-resume and funding in the same session. The program agreement, including the statement that the sponsor has exclusive legal control over contributed assets, MUST be accepted once by click-accept recording agreement version, timestamp, authenticated principal and channel; wet signatures MUST NOT be required. View-only participants MUST NOT be required to complete identity proofing (RCD-023). Facts the donor declines to confirm MUST be re-entered and re-verified under the normal checks. Prefill is a convenience, not proof of identity: each prefilled value MUST carry its source, retrieval time and the purpose and consent under which it was obtained, and MAY be used only within its source's freshness window for that purpose. Prefill MUST NOT satisfy identity proofing, and a prefilled value MUST NOT silently overwrite a verified value: a conflict MUST open a confirmation step showing both values and their sources.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a verified address on file and a different address supplied by the identity provider
added_acceptance_criteria.then: both values are shown with their sources, the verified value is unchanged until the donor confirms, and identity proofing still runs

revised_statement: The system MUST classify instructions as conflicting when their scopes overlap and cannot both execute, and MUST resolve them by the precedence rules: explicit author-confirmed supersession for the same author; the fund's recorded authority grant for different holders, taken from the fund agreement and never inferred from marital or relationship status (Any-one only where the agreement explicitly grants it, otherwise AllRequired); invalidity after verified death/incapacity; latest sponsor-approved plan version. Unresolvable conflicts MUST hold the consequential effect and open a sponsor case. Capacity for each instruction MUST be reserved atomically at commit, so that concurrently committed instructions cannot together exceed available capacity; the instruction that cannot be reserved is held as conflicting.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: spouses holding a fund whose agreement grants no explicit any-one authority
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the grant waits for the other holder's agreement

added_acceptance_criteria.given: two holders with any-one authority and $10,000 available
added_acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one is reserved and the other is HeldConflict with a sponsor case

revised_statement: In addition to RR-REQ-X-007-r1: (1) A scheduled deep review that finds all required evidence current and passing under the active policy version SHALL renew the common verification automatically, recording the policy version as the approving authority, with no human sign-off where the sponsor's delegated policy permits (OD-01). (2) Renewal SHALL start no later than the FreshnessPolicy refresh lead time, with load-spreading, so that an expired deep review holds new approvals only when renewal has failed. (3) Event-triggered revalidation (RR-UNB-EXT-028-r1) SHALL reset the deep-review clock only when it performs a full review. (4) A verification reused by a second sponsor SHALL NOT trigger new routine vetting; that sponsor's policy overlay and per-grant reliance snapshot SHALL still be evaluated. (5) Automatically renewed verifications SHALL be independently reviewed after the fact, without blocking grants, under the common risk-based sampling policy of UNB-XIN-CLM-005 (as revised 2026-11-24): each stratum declares a confidence level and tolerable error rate from which the sample size follows. A fixed sample of 30 MAY be used only as an exploratory pilot and SHALL NOT be reported as assurance (zero errors in 30 still leaves an upper 95% error bound near 10%). (6) The platform SHALL report renewal success rate, evidence reuse ratio (grants per verification), time-to-detect material adverse events, false-hold and false-clear rates.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a stratum with a declared 95% confidence and 3% tolerable error rate
added_acceptance_criteria.then: its size follows from those parameters, not from a fixed 30, and the report states the error bound achieved

revised_statement: For each legal entity and each accounting basis there MUST be exactly one authoritative book, which MAY be kept in Unbound or in an external system designated book of record (UNB-XIN-ACC-010); Unbound MUST NOT be required to own the general ledger. The accrual-basis (US GAAP) book is the primary basis. Any other basis required by a named filing or contract MUST be produced as a derived report with typed reconciling items to the authoritative GAAP book, not as a parallel posted book. Where the authoritative book is external, Unbound's records MUST reconcile to it and MUST NOT be treated as a second authoritative book.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a sponsor whose external ERP is designated book of record for the general ledger
added_acceptance_criteria.then: they reconcile to the external book, and Unbound posts no parallel authoritative ledger

revised_statement: Segregation of duties MUST be enforced for: posting-rule version approval, manual journals, bank and payee master changes, reconciliation sign-off, close certification and payment release; the approver of each MUST differ from its preparer. Journals generated by an approved posting-rule version from authoritative events MUST NOT require per-journal human approval. AI cannot approve its own accounting actions or any action listed above. Reporting scope: the sponsor's external ERP is the default home of entity-wide financial statements but MUST NOT be mandatory. Unbound MUST support DAF program reporting and, where configured as authoritative general ledger, the reports that book requires, without building generic ERP functions (accounts payable, procurement, budgeting, payroll, fixed assets).

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a sponsor without an external ERP that configures Unbound as authoritative general ledger for its DAF program
added_acceptance_criteria.then: program and entity statements for that book are produced and no accounts payable or payroll module is required

revised_statement: Every API and event contract MUST declare a tier (Internal, Partner, Public) and a semantic version. Breaking changes, detected in CI from generated schemas (UNB-RCN-ARC-001) plus annotated semantic changes, MUST increment the major version. A superseded major version of a Public contract MUST remain available for at least 18 months, and of a Partner contract for at least 12 months or the partner contract term if longer, after the successor is generally available; Internal contracts follow the release lifecycle with no minimum. Each contract version MUST carry a lifecycle state (Preview, GA, Deprecated, Sunset) and a published migration guide before it is deprecated. An emergency exception for security or legal compulsion MAY shorten the period only with recorded approval, notice to every registered consumer and a mitigation path. Deprecated versions MUST be served with Deprecation and Sunset metadata on every response, and notice MUST be sent to every registered consumer at announcement, 90 days and 30 days before sunset. A sunset MUST NOT strand in-flight objects: requests accepted under the old version MUST be completed and their status remain queryable. Rate limits MUST be declared per tier and per tenant and returned in response metadata.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: Public contract v1 superseded by v2, generally available on 1 January 2027
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it cannot be earlier than 1 July 2028 unless an approved emergency exception and consumer notices are recorded

revised_statement: In addition to RR-UNB-EXT-004-r1: a potential match dispositioned as a false positive by an authorized human SHALL be recorded with the subject's identity attributes, the list entry identifier and the list-entry version, and SHALL be reused automatically for subsequent screenings of the same subject against the same list-entry version. The reuse SHALL be invalidated when the subject's identity attributes (name, address, country, identifiers) or the list entry change, or after a counsel-set maximum age. Reuse SHALL NOT apply to true matches, unresolved potential matches, or a different list entry. Name similarity alone SHALL NOT cause an adverse determination. Reuse of a human false-positive disposition is limited to the sponsor legal entity that made it, unless counsel records a cross-sponsor reliance basis (SPD-ADV-002, SPF-ADV-007). A sanctions false-positive disposition SHALL NOT be used as, or imply, a charity eligibility determination: eligibility follows RR-REQ-X-007 (full deep review at most every 180 days and earlier on an event-triggered invalidation), and payment release SHALL use sanctions screening current at release (RR-UNB-EXT-028). Counsel sets the maximum age of a disposition and any cross-sponsor reuse; until counsel records a maximum age, dispositions SHALL NOT be reused.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a recorded false-positive disposition for the officers of charity X
added_acceptance_criteria.when: an eligibility check for X runs
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the disposition does not satisfy any eligibility requirement

added_acceptance_criteria.given: no counsel-recorded maximum age
added_acceptance_criteria.when: the same subject is screened again
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the prior disposition is not reused and the potential match goes to review

revised_statement: The system SHALL monitor source updates, status changes, leadership changes, financial-filing changes, enforcement events and entity relationships for every charity with an open grant, active schedule, unreleased payment or grant in the prior 24 months. Each detected change SHALL be classified by a versioned, counsel-approved MaterialityTable into: (a) Material-Adverse (e.g. revocation, sanctions listing, dissolution, bankruptcy, EIN change, successor designation, supporting-organization type change, change matching a sponsor DiscretionaryGrantPolicy criterion) -> publish a hold to the hold registry within the policy's detection SLA, re-evaluate only impacted grants and schedules (UNB-GEX-019), apply UNB-XIN-NPG-005 effects, and open one case per charity and reason; (b) Material-Neutral (name change same EIN, address change) -> apply deterministic effects without a case; (c) Informational (leadership change, routine filing) -> update evidence with no hold, no case and no human task. Classification rules SHALL be deterministic; AI may propose a classification only for unstructured sources and the proposal SHALL NOT publish or clear a hold. Each monitored source MUST declare its freshness: its publication lag and, per decision (approval, release), the maximum age of evidence accepted. Decisions MUST use cached verified evidence within the approved window and MUST NOT require a live provider call for every payment; when evidence is older than the window or the source is unavailable, the decision MUST fail safe (hold, never pass). Detection SLAs MUST be stated relative to the source's publication, not to the underlying event.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: IRS status evidence retrieved 10 hours ago under a 24-hour release window
added_acceptance_criteria.then: no live call is made and release proceeds

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a provider outage and evidence 30 hours old under a 24-hour window
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the release is held with reason StaleEvidence

revised_statement: The sponsor MAY approve, modify under policy with a recorded explanation, or reject/hold a proposed funding allocation. Renewed advisor consent MUST be requested only when the modification changes the recipient, the award amount or the payment timing beyond policy tolerance; a change limited to which sponsor-held assets fund an unchanged grant MAY proceed with record and notice only when all of the following hold: the fund's investment exposure stays within its approved allocation; no restriction attached to the assets is breached; tax and accounting consequences for the fund and the donor are unchanged; and an authorized funding instruction or sponsor policy permits the substitution. Otherwise the sponsor MUST obtain the advisor's approval before proceeding.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a funding substitution that moves the fund outside its approved allocation band
added_acceptance_criteria.then: advisor approval is requested before execution

revised_statement: Straight-through (Tier-1 policy) approval MUST be enabled per rule version only. Each enabled rule version MUST declare: the low-risk criteria it applies; its DoA entry; monitoring signals (STP rate, post-approval hold/reversal rate, sampled error rate from UNB-XIN-CLM-005 with confidence interval, override count); a threshold for each signal; the trigger claim; and the response, which MUST be suspension of that rule version to its declared fallback (UNB-SMP-ARX-001). The system MUST open a reassessment case for the rule owner when any threshold is crossed and MUST open a trigger-reassessment case when no threshold has been crossed for 12 consecutive months while override or hold counts rose by more than a declared amount. Batching MUST NOT carry approval authority (UNB-XIN-EVA-011). Sampling for each enabled rule version MUST follow the common risk-based sampling policy of UNB-XIN-CLM-005 (as revised 2026-11-24). Any sampled error MUST trigger independent review of the item, escalation to the rule owner and a larger sample for that rule version until the error bound is back within tolerance.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: one sampled error in rule version 7
added_acceptance_criteria.then: a remediation case and rule-owner escalation exist and the next period's sample for version 7 is larger

revised_statement: Recovery objectives MUST be defined and approved before architecture acceptance and verified by restore test before production use; the values below are candidates until that approval. Unbound MUST define recovery objectives per data class, not per capability, in one versioned table, at minimum: (C0) acknowledged authoritative financial/security commits (ledger, reservations, approvals, holds, payee/destination versions, authority, payment send intents): RPO 0, RTO <= 4 hours, restore to a single consistency point across all C0 stores; (C1) issued document artifacts and evidence: RPO 0 for issued artifacts, RTO <= 24 hours; (C2) operational records (cases, notes, communications history): RPO <= 15 minutes, RTO <= 24 hours; (C3) rebuildable projections, search indexes, caches, embeddings: no backup required if rebuild from C0 is tested, RTO <= 24 hours; (C4) telemetry and non-evidentiary logs: best effort. Each tenant contract MUST reference this table; a tenant MAY buy stricter RTO only with a matching isolation profile. Every class MUST have a restore drill at least annually per isolation profile in use, including tenant-selective restore where the profile claims it, and payment release MUST stay blocked after any restore until C0 consistency and provider reconciliation pass (REQ-X-006). No acknowledged financial fact (class C0) may be lost by a recovery unless an approved recovery procedure states the loss semantics, the compensating records and the customer notice.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: an architecture acceptance review
added_acceptance_criteria.when: the recovery table lacks approval or a passing C0 restore drill
added_acceptance_criteria.then: acceptance is refused

revised_statement: Before a platform-maintained policy-pack version is published, the system MUST shadow-evaluate it against each adopting sponsor's decisions of at least the prior 90 days using pinned evidence, and MUST produce a per-sponsor diff of changed outcomes. Publication MUST require sign-off by the pack owner when any sponsor's changed-outcome share exceeds a declared threshold. Activation MUST be staged: the version becomes effective for at most one sponsor (or one declared cohort) first and for others only after the first stage has processed a declared representative volume covering each risk stratum the change affects, no reassessment trigger has fired, and rollback of that version has been rehearsed; elapsed time alone (for example seven days) MUST NOT satisfy the observation criterion. Each pack parameter MUST declare either an ordering (so "tighten only" is checkable) or an enumerated set of approved alternatives. Rollback to the prior version MUST be a single versioned action.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: seven days elapsed but only 12 items processed in an affected high-risk stratum whose declared volume is 50
added_acceptance_criteria.when: promotion to the next cohort is requested
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused

revised_statement: Each automated decision path (policy grant approval, charity status refresh, automated reconciliation matching, automated contribution acceptance) MUST declare a fallback mode of Hold or HumanQueue and an expected human minutes per item. When the path is suspended or its inputs are stale, the system MUST apply the declared fallback, MUST notify affected donors/advisors/charities with a reason class and an expected next-update time, and MUST compute and display the projected backlog clearance time against the rostered capacity for the reviewing role. The system MUST NOT release, approve or match any held item solely because of its age or backlog size. During a suspension, donors, advisors and charities MAY keep read-only access to their records only while the confidentiality and integrity of the data shown remain trustworthy; if either is in doubt, affected parties MUST be switched to a status-only channel showing the reason class and expected next update, without account data.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a suspension caused by suspected data corruption in fund balances
added_acceptance_criteria.then: only the status-only channel is shown, with no balances

revised_statement: Every Next Best Action (NBA) shown on a dashboard, work queue or customer home MUST be generated from a registered Intervention type that declares: triggering condition (deterministic rule or metric threshold from the metric registry); evidence fields cited; expected outcome; ranking inputs (harm avoided or value protected, deadline proximity, legal clock, customer impact, effort) combined by a published deterministic ranking rule in which hard legal deadlines and imminent-harm conditions are constraints, not weights: such items rank ahead of all others, a collision where two cannot both be completed in time by available authorized principals MUST be escalated to the accountable executive, and every item MUST rise in rank with age so that none is starved; the domain command it opens and that command's authority class (UNB-RCN-PLT-005). An NBA MUST be shown as actionable only if the viewer currently holds authority for the command; otherwise it MUST be shown as unavailable with the reason and the role that can act. Selecting an NBA MUST open the authoritative command with re-checked state and MUST NOT execute A3 or higher actions directly. AI MAY explain or draft evidence for an NBA but MUST NOT change its rank.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: two statutory-deadline items due tomorrow and one authorized principal available
added_acceptance_criteria.then: both rank first and a collision escalation is opened for the accountable executive

revised_statement: Before activating a sponsor onboarding, an inbound book migration or a growth campaign that adds more than a configured share (default 10%) of active accounts within any 60-business-day window, the platform SHALL run the capacity forecast (UNB-XIN-ECO-017) including the added steady-state volume and the declared one-off migration work, and SHALL require an approver acknowledgment recording the projected SLA attainment per queue, projected peak backlog and days to clear whenever any queue's projected SLA attainment is below its mandatory minimum service floor or projected backlog does not clear within 30 business days. Reductions in cost per account attributable to account growth SHALL be reported separately and SHALL NOT be credited as verified savings under UNB-XIN-ECO-015/019. Each queue's floor MUST be a named metric (for example the share of items decided within the profile's target time) with a mandatory minimum approved by the accountable executive before activation; contract service tiers MAY set higher targets but MUST NOT lower or replace the internal minimum. Until the metric and minimum are approved, the acknowledgment is required for every activation in scope.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a contract tier promising 80% while the approved internal minimum is 90%
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the acknowledgment is required

revised_statement: For each reserved decision class in the authority matrix (UNB-RCN-PLT-005) that has a service-level clock, the platform MUST compute daily, for the next 20 business days (configurable), an AuthorityCoverage record: the set of principals holding a valid DoA entry for that class (UNB-XIN-ERP-005) who are scheduled available, minus those excluded by recorded absence; and it MUST test whether the class's distinctness requirement can be met (e.g. two approvers excluding the releaser for NotReceived; payee approver ≠ releaser) using per-item SoD history rather than fixed role-per-person assignments. When coverage fails for any day, the platform MUST open a CoverageGap work item (class FiduciaryGovernance) for the accountable executive at least 10 business days before the day (or immediately if later), listing pre-authorized backup delegates that would close the gap. The platform MUST NOT relax SoD, auto-approve, or extend an approver's authority to close a gap; items that cannot be decided wait with their SLA status and customer notice per their profile. The required coverage depth for each class (single or double absence) MUST be derived from the class's criticality (legal clock, financial exposure, customer harm) and forecast peak workload, not from the calendar alone; year-end and other forecast peaks MUST be run as stress scenarios with simultaneous absences.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a class with a statutory clock and a December forecast at 3x normal volume
added_acceptance_criteria.then: double-absence coverage is required and the year-end stress scenario runs

revised_statement: For a fund whose FundAttribution function is designated Shadow under UNB-XIN-ACC-010, grantable capacity MUST be computed as: the fund's available balance in the latest external snapshot accepted as complete under UNB-XIN-EVA-004 (with its as-of watermark) minus all Unbound reservations and released-unsettled grants committed after that watermark minus accrued-unposted fees reported by the external system. Reservations MUST be committed in Unbound's reservation table under the same locking rules as Authoritative funds. When the snapshot watermark is older than the sponsor-configured staleness limit (default 1 business day) the system MUST block capacity increases and new reservations above a sponsor-configured de minimis amount, while permitting protective actions. Each daily reconciliation break between the external balance and (prior snapshot - Unbound-originated settled outflows since) MUST open a reconciliation case and MUST freeze new reservations for the affected fund until resolved or accepted by the controller. By default Unbound MUST support import and comparison of externally kept fund attribution (reconciliation reports and breaks) without maintaining an optional duplicate attribution ledger; Shadow FundAttribution is enabled per sponsor only after a recorded demand decision showing the external system is book of record for fund attribution.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a sponsor with no recorded Shadow demand decision
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is compared and reconciled, and no duplicate attribution ledger is created

revised_statement: Every business day the system MUST ingest bank activity for each sponsor disbursement, clearing and operating account linked to Unbound and match every debit to exactly one authorized platform instruction or to a configured expected-debit class (bank fee, sweep, return); any unmatched debit MUST open a high-severity incident within one hour of ingestion, notify two independent sponsor roles and place a protective hold on further releases from that account until an authorized human classifies it; ACH debit block or filter status for disbursement accounts MUST be recorded and attested quarterly. Grant disbursement accounts MUST carry an ACH debit block allowing only named bank-fee company IDs; processors MUST settle to a separate contribution clearing account where only the processor's company ID may debit (XID-BNK-008). Prior-day bank activity alone MUST NOT establish spendable capacity: capacity MUST net Unbound reservations and released-unsettled payments committed after the latest bank-data watermark, and each rail MUST declare the maximum bank-data age at which new releases may proceed; older data blocks new releases on that rail while permitting protective actions.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a rail whose declared maximum bank-data age is one business day and data that is two business days old
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is blocked while holds and recalls remain possible

revised_statement: A reconsideration Case MUST: (a) be accepted only within a sponsor-configured filing window (default 60 days from decision notice, configurable, and extended where law, a disability accommodation or a documented failure to deliver the decision notice requires) and at most once per decision unless new material evidence is supplied; (b) be decided by an authorized reviewer who neither made nor prepared the original decision and does not report to the person who did; (c) re-evaluate on current policy and all evidence including new submissions, without deference to the original outcome, while preserving the original decision record unchanged (SM-0); (d) have a decision-time target from its profile (default 30 calendar days) with notice of extension; (e) end in one of: upheld, reversed, modified, withdrawn; (f) where the original decision concerned shared charity vetting, be decided on the platform vetting record by the vetting authority and only then re-run sponsor grant gates, never altering a sponsor's discretionary decision without sponsor action. This revision supersedes the competing 90-day default (SPD-ENT-002, XID-CLM-001); the original and reconsideration records are both preserved.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a request filed on day 61 with no qualifying exception
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is declined as out of window with the reason and any other recourse

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a request filed on day 75 where the decision notice was not delivered until day 20
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted under the delivery-failure exception

revised_statement: Each month Unbound MUST draw a stratified random sample of closed grant approvals (straight-through and human), charity vetting determinations and gift acceptances, sized under the common risk-based sampling policy (each stratum declares a confidence level and tolerable error rate from which the size follows; higher-risk strata are sampled more heavily; a fixed 30 is exploratory only; any error escalates and enlarges the next sample for that stratum), for independent review by a qualified reviewer who did not make the decisions. Results MUST record error type and severity; any error MUST open a remediation case for the affected item and a learning signal (REQ-X-042). The error rate with confidence interval MUST be reported alongside the STP rate. This policy is the single sampling policy referenced by RR-REQ-X-007, RR-UNB-GRANT-030 and other sampling requirements.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: two strata with different declared tolerable error rates
added_acceptance_criteria.then: each stratum's size follows its own parameters

revised_statement: For operations whose estimated cost exceeds a configured threshold (defaults: AI agent run > $2; international grant ED/ER review; wire or check where ACH is available to the recipient; complex-asset liquidation), the platform SHALL produce a CostQuote {operation, estimate low/expected/high, components, bearer, rate-card versions, validUntil} before execution. CostQuotes SHALL be advisory: they SHALL NOT block, skip or reorder any legally or policy-required control step, SHALL NOT change recipient payment method selection, and SHALL NOT alter sponsor decisions. Where a configured service charge will be charged to a fund, the donor-facing quote SHALL be shown before affirmation and the charge SHALL not exceed the quoted high value without new affirmation. If the actual charge would exceed the accepted maximum (the quoted high value the donor affirmed), the platform MUST obtain new affirmation before charging the excess or the sponsor MUST absorb the difference. No service charge may be made for an accommodation required for accessibility.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a quote with a $40 high value affirmed by the donor and an actual cost of $55
added_acceptance_criteria.then: either new affirmation is recorded or only $40 is charged to the fund and $15 is absorbed by the sponsor

revised_statement: Cost views SHALL be scoped: sponsor users see only their sponsor's attributed costs plus their share of shared-platform costs with the allocation method disclosed; cross-sponsor benchmarks SHALL require at least 5 contributing sponsors and suppress any cell where one sponsor exceeds 60% of the total; labour costs SHALL be shown at pool/team/activity level with minimum group size 5 and SHALL NOT be shown per named worker or used to rank individuals. The minimums of 5 sponsors, 60% dominance and group size 5 are experimental minimums for testing, not release authorization: before any cross-sponsor benchmark or labour-cost view is released, it MUST pass differencing, longitudinal (repeated-release) and collusion re-identification tests approved by the privacy owner.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a benchmark meeting the 5-sponsor minimum that fails a differencing test across two releases
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused

revised_statement: The fee engine MUST compute every fund-level fee daily on the daily balance of the declared FeeBase, using actual/365 (actual/366 in leap years) unless the schedule version declares otherwise, and MUST post the computed fee once per assessment period declared in the schedule (monthly or quarterly), not daily. The computation MUST segment at each of: fund activation, schedule-version effective date, program transfer, successor split or merge, closure trigger and migration cutover; each segment uses the schedule version and fee base in effect for that segment. Treatment of a minimum fee in a partial period (prorated by the same day count, charged in full, or not charged) MUST be declared in the schedule version from the sponsor's contract; there is no proration default. In the closing period no minimum fee beyond the computed actual-day fee may be assessed unless the schedule version discloses a closing minimum authorized by contract. Grantable capacity MUST subtract fees computed but not yet posted. The assessed amount MUST NOT exceed the fund's available balance net of reservations and approved-unpaid grants at assessment; any shortfall MUST be recorded as a waived amount with reason MinimumShortfall and MUST NOT create a receivable from any donor or participant. Recomputing any assessed fee from stored inputs MUST reproduce it exactly. The daily computation MUST run in chunks so that no transaction locks more than 5,000 fund rows, and concurrent grant approvals MUST stay within their latency SLO while it runs (benchmark report 18: a single-transaction batch stalled approvals up to 347 ms at 100,000 funds and about 12 s at 1.42 million).

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a fund closing on day 20 of a quarter under a schedule that discloses no closing minimum
added_acceptance_criteria.then: only the actual-day fee for days 1-20 is charged

revised_statement: Each advisor instruction MUST carry a conflict scope key (fund, instruction kind, and target: charity, schedule, investment allocation or transfer). On commit, the handler MUST, in the same transaction, check for open instructions with the same scope from a different principal that request an incompatible outcome; if found, both MUST move to HeldConflict and a case opened for the sponsor, unless the fund's recorded authority matrix (the same matrix used for joint holders under RR-ADM-023-r2) resolves it deterministically; any-one authority MUST NOT be implied, so absent an explicit grant all authorized holders must agree and ambiguity holds the instruction. A one-off instruction for a scheduled occurrence MUST take precedence over the standing instruction only for that occurrence when sponsor policy says so. Every consequential command MUST compare the fund's authority epoch at commit with the epoch at recommendation; if it advanced (revocation, death notice, successor activation), unapproved recommendations MUST be held, and approved-reserved grants MUST follow the sponsor's in-flight policy.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a two-advisor fund with no explicit any-one grant
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is held until the other advisor agrees

revised_statement: A message broker, separately deployed service or second authoritative store MUST NOT be introduced unless an ADR presents reproducible measurements on the selected managed PostgreSQL showing at least one of: (a) required peak authoritative commit rate exceeds 50% of benchmarked sustainable capacity of the largest sponsor database after indexing, partitioning and connection pooling; (b) p99 outbox dispatch lag exceeds 60 seconds for three consecutive peak days after tuning; (c) a contractual or regulatory clause requires an isolation profile that cannot be met inside the sponsor database (UNB-RCN-PLT-012). The benchmark MUST model the year-end peak of the largest expected sponsor using the documented volume method. Before any instance size is selected or benchmarked for acceptance, the ADR MUST state the target workload (peak commit rate, data volume, concurrency), SLOs, RPO/RTO (RR-UNB-RES-003-r2) and cost envelope, and the benchmark MUST include failover and contention scenarios (concurrent batch jobs during peak).

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a benchmark ADR without a stated cost envelope or failover run
added_acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused

revised_statement: Every sponsor discretionary hold or decline not required by law MUST cite a criterion from a board-approved, versioned DiscretionaryGrantPolicy, record the evidence class (allegation, pending matter, adjudicated finding or regulator action per UNB-EXT-005), the approving authority, scope (recipient, purpose, period) and a review date no later than the policy's maximum, and MUST produce a donor-facing reason class from the policy's approved wording. On review date the hold MUST either be renewed by the same authority with new evidence or released automatically. The system MUST produce on demand a consistency report listing all discretionary holds by criterion, evidence class and duration. An allegation alone, including an indictment, MUST NOT place a hold automatically. A temporary discretionary hold MAY be placed only where documented evidence shows credible risk under an approved DiscretionaryGrantPolicy criterion, for a time-bound period with independent review before any renewal; holds required by law are separate and unaffected. Any proposal allowing holds only on adjudicated findings is to be reconciled with this rule.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a news report of an indictment of a charity officer and no other evidence
added_acceptance_criteria.then: no hold is placed and the event is recorded for review

revised_statement: Every authoritative event, outbox message, inbox record, audit record and telemetry span MUST carry an immutable envelope with TenantId, LegalSponsorId, ProgramId (where applicable), a tenant-scoped sequence number, CorrelationId and CausationId. CorrelationId and CausationId MUST be generated within the tenant and MUST NOT reference an event of another tenant; the only permitted cross-tenant references are declared inter-cell contract messages (global holds, shared charity facts, sponsor-to-sponsor transfers) which carry both tenants' references explicitly. Persisting an event without a TenantId MUST fail. Tenant migration MUST preserve event ids, tenant sequence and envelope values unchanged. For global holds a freshness watermark alone MUST NOT be relied on to close the race between a hold and a payment: every irreversible dispatch MUST re-check authorization against the hold registry atomically with a fencing token at dispatch, dispatch MUST be idempotent, and payments in flight when a hold is published MUST be reconciled and stopped or recalled where still possible.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a global hold published while a payment is between approval and dispatch
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the fenced re-check refuses dispatch and the payment is held

revised_statement: Unbound MUST emit an append-only UsageRecord per tenant and program for: authoritative storage bytes, document/object storage bytes, API calls by tier, background compute seconds, AI model calls with input/output tokens and model id, external provider calls by provider and billable unit, outbound messages by channel, and human work minutes on WorkItems. Shared infrastructure cost MUST be allocated monthly to tenants by declared allocation keys versioned per period. Monthly metered totals MUST reconcile to infrastructure and provider invoices within 5 percent or create a finance exception. Usage records MUST NOT be inputs to authorization or to fund-level fee accrual; fees remain governed by sponsor fee policy. Allocation keys MUST use the same causal cost-attribution model as UNB-XIN-ECO-001 and XID-ECO-004. Causal attribution (what consumed the cost) MUST be kept separate from contract billing (what a customer is charged) and from showback, and each cost amount MUST be allocated exactly once per period with a reconciliation proving no double allocation.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a month's provider invoice
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the sum allocated across tenants equals the invoice and no line is allocated twice

revised_statement: Unbound MUST classify as a complaint any Contact in which a party expresses dissatisfaction with the sponsor's or platform's service, decision, communication or conduct, regardless of channel or wording, and MUST open a Case of kind complaint. The complaint profile MUST define: acknowledgement within a sponsor-configured period (default 2 business days); substantive response target (default 15 business days) with extension notice; mandatory taxonomy code; flag regulator-originated (state AG, IRS, other) which routes to counsel and cannot be closed by service staff; closure requiring outcome, customer response sent, and root-cause code. Complaints MUST NOT be closed by AI. A complaint about a decision MUST offer the reconsideration path where one exists. Each complaint MUST track end-to-end elapsed time from first contact to closure alongside the internal SLA clock; the SLA clock MAY pause only with a documented reason (for example awaiting the complainant), and no pause extends any statutory or regulatory deadline.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a regulator-originated complaint paused 5 days awaiting the complainant
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the deadline is unchanged and both elapsed time and paused SLA time are reported

revised_statement: Every policy parameter that changes approval, eligibility, agent permissions, financial limits or risk MUST be versioned and automatically back-tested against the historical corpus before publication. A material change to financial controls, eligibility, agent permissions, financial limits or customer rights MUST require independent approval, with author different from approver, whether it loosens or tightens. Single-approver handling is allowed only for changes classified low-risk under an independently approved change policy; mixed or ambiguous changes are material. Classification of a change as tightening MUST be computed, not self-declared. Back-testing MUST use representative history plus synthetic edge cases.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a change that lowers a grant limit so that queued grants would miss deadlines
added_acceptance_criteria.then: independent approval is required and the author cannot self-approve

revised_statement: Unbound MUST maintain a critical-vendor register recording assurance type, legal entity and report period; MUST require a bridge letter when the period end is more than 3 months old and mark assurance Expired after 12 months; and MUST map every complementary user entity control to an internal control owner before the vendor is marked Assured. AI may extract report metadata for human confirmation only. The 3- and 12-month values are provisional monitoring defaults, not audit standards; the sponsor's auditor confirms reliance criteria. A bridge letter MUST NOT be recorded as extending independent assurance. The register MUST track coverage gap, report scope, opinion type, exceptions, complementary user entity controls and any time-limited risk acceptance; an adverse opinion or expired risk acceptance MUST change the vendor's status, and suspending a critical vendor MUST follow a recorded risk-based continuity decision.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a vendor with a bridge letter and an unmapped complementary user entity control
added_acceptance_criteria.then: the vendor is not Assured and the coverage gap is shown

revised_statement: Every external provider adapter that incurs cost SHALL emit VendorCostRecords in a FOCUS-aligned schema (BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ListCost, BillingCurrency, ChargeCategory, ChargePeriodStart/End, SubAccountId=sponsor/tenant where known, ConsumedQuantity/Unit, Tags including cost-object keys, x_Bearer in {Fund, Sponsor, Platform, Partner}, x_SourceInvoiceRef). Where a provider meters per request, the adapter SHALL attach the domain correlation id at call time so the cost is DirectMetered. Monthly invoices SHALL be ingested and reconciled to metered sums; differences go to residual. FOCUS 1.4 (ratified 4 June 2026) is the internal mapping target; providers may supply other FOCUS versions or none and are mapped by version-aware adapters, and low-volume vendors may use invoice-only ingestion. Native invoice and usage provenance MUST be preserved, Unbound MUST NOT claim FOCUS conformance for a subset mapping, and later FOCUS versions are adopted only by recorded decision.

added_acceptance_criteria.given: a provider supplying FOCUS 1.2 data
added_acceptance_criteria.then: a version-aware adapter maps it to the 1.4 target and keeps the native invoice reference
